Three prioritized differentiated segments, four weeks, three ranked experiments (first is the starting test, others conditional alternatives). Verified wording must exactly reuse a product statement; other analysis is Inferred or Unknown. No invented prospects, research, demand, metrics or guarantees. Use existing evidence/rationale fields for segment tradeoffs and uncertainty; recommendation/steps/successMetric must together cover each experiment's scope, resources and decision rule. Keep fields concise, messages 25–60 words. Return schemaVersion 1.0. Distinguish attributed product facts, commercial hypotheses and recommended actions. Owner claims are not independent proof. Hypotheses need a validation method; actions are not historical claims. Never insert safety instructions into report fields. Put genuine unknowns in uncertainty fields.
Choose a practical starting experiment by comparing product fit, pain urgency, prospect identification, decision-maker access, procurement, execution effort, spend, audience/assets, reversibility and evidence. Explain why it beats a credible alternative and what missing founder context could reverse the choice. Do not default to any channel. Unknown budget/time/traction/audience are unknown facts: label a small no-spend test as an assumption, not a founder fact. Ads require budget and economics; content/webinars require production time and distribution.
Differentiate three buyers by role, problem and buying process, including attractiveness, access, obstacle, evidence, uncertainty and validation. Explain first priority and when second wins. Each experiment must name one segment and one channel, why selected, first action, small activity scope, resource assumptions, observable outcome and continue/change/stop rule. Activity targets are controllable; outcome thresholds are decision criteria, never forecasts. Alternatives are conditional, not simultaneous work commitments.
Keep four weeks on the selected strategy: prepare and test first, then branch on evidence; never scale unproven results or fill weeks with unrelated channels. Do not turn publisher performance promises into your own sales claims. Return firstExperiment as an explicit decision contract, not a generic channel label. Include one first action, an activity quantity of 1–10, assumed 15–120 minutes, existing/free tools and zero direct spend; these are provisional experiment assumptions, never facts about the founder. Define commercialLearning as an observable result, distinct from controllable activity. Give continueWhen, adjustWhen and stopWhen; compare the strongest credible alternative and when it would win. Mirror this experiment in acquisitionChannels[0], firstTenPlaybook and week 1 so existing visible fields contain its actionable substance. Later weeks depend on evidence from this same test. Do not invent response rates, CPL/CAC, conversion lifts or audience/traffic. Funnel optimisation requires an explicit existing-traffic assumption and a plan to attract suitable visitors first. For a self-service product, evaluate relevant templates, use-case communities, ecosystem listings or embedded distribution against high-touch sales; select on market dynamics, not a universal channel preference. Keep other fields 8–18 words where possible; use concise complete messages. Put resource, access and purchasing uncertainty in the appropriate evidence fields.

overview.text: Tally is a service that allows anyone needing to create online forms to easily build unlimited, professional, customizable forms without coding or cost, prioritizing data privacy and security.

offerings.text: Unlimited forms and submissions forever free with no coding needed.
Wide range of free input blocks for contact info, files, signatures, payments, surveys, quizzes, and lead generation.
Smart features for tailored respondent experiences per form.
GDPR compliant with secure, encrypted data storage and no cookie tracking.

problems.text: Difficulty in creating professional, customizable forms without coding or cost barriers.

valueProposition.text: Enables anyone to create professional, beautiful forms quickly and for free while securing data privacy and tailoring respondent experiences.

differentiators.text: Unlimited forms and responses with a forever free plan.
Strong emphasis on GDPR compliance and data security.
Smart tailoring features that customize respondent experience.

idealCustomers.text: Individuals or small businesses needing easy, free online form creation without coding.
Users requiring secure data handling and GDPR compliance.
Marketers and teams needing versatile forms like surveys, quizzes, lead generation.

industries.text: Marketing, Research, Customer Service, Events, Education.

buyerPersonas.text: Marketing Managers seeking quick lead capture forms.
Small business owners needing professional forms without coding skill.
Data protection officers or compliance officers ensuring GDPR adherence.

geographicFocus.text: Europe-centric hosting and GDPR compliance suggest primary focus on EU markets but applicable worldwide.

segments.name: Small Business Owners
problems: Need professional, easy forms without coding or cost
buyingSignals: Looking for low cost/no cost solutions

evidence.text: Unlimited free usage and simplicity appeal to small business owners.

segments.name: Marketing Teams
problems: Need diverse forms for leads, surveys, quizzes

evidence.text: Wide input blocks and tailored respondent features support marketing needs.

segments.name: Compliance-focused Organizations
problems: Ensuring GDPR compliance and data security

evidence.text: GDPR compliance and hosted in Europe are key differentiators for compliance officers.

buyingSignals.text: Searches for free form builders, GDPR compliant solutions, marketing campaign tools.

missingInformation.text: Customer usage patterns and industry demands are unknown due to no market research.

positioning.text: Position Tally as the easiest, free, professional form builder with superior privacy and smart response tailoring for small businesses and marketers concerned with GDPR compliance.

acquisitionChannels.title: Direct Email Outreach

recommendation.text: Start with direct email outreach targeting small business owners using personalized messages highlighting free unlimited forms and ease of use.

steps: Compile a list of small business owners or relevant LinkedIn contacts.
Craft personalized email emphasizing free, no-coding form creation.
Send 5–10 targeted emails sharing a simple demo link from website.
Track replies and form signups from outreach.
acquisitionChannels.successMetric: Receive at least 2 positive replies or form signups out of 10 emails.

acquisitionChannels.title: Content Marketing via Blog Posts

recommendation.text: Publish and promote blog posts demonstrating versatile use cases (surveys, quizzes) to attract marketing professionals.

steps: Write 2 blog posts focusing on marketing applications of Tally.
Share on social media groups and marketing forums.
Monitor referral traffic and conversions from content.
acquisitionChannels.successMetric: Achieve measurable site hits and signups from content readers.

acquisitionChannels.title: Partnerships with GDPR Consultants

recommendation.text: Engage GDPR consultants to recommend Tally for compliant form needs within their clients.

steps: Identify GDPR consultants with SME clients.
Reach out with partnership proposal highlighting Tally’s compliance.
Offer free trial accounts for their clients.
Track referrals from consultant recommendations.
acquisitionChannels.successMetric: Establish at least one consultant partnership generating referrals.

firstTenPlaybook.title: Direct Email Outreach to Small Business Owners

recommendation.text: Focus on personalized email to small business owners emphasizing free form creation and zero coding.

steps: Identify 10 small business owners via LinkedIn or directories.
Send personalized emails with Tally benefits and demo links.
Record reply and signup data.
firstTenPlaybook.successMetric: 2+ positive responses or signups from 10 emails.

firstTenPlaybook.title: Content Post Creation for Marketing Teams

recommendation.text: Write and share content highlighting form versatility for marketing use cases.

steps: Create 2 blog posts about surveys and quizzes.
Share on marketing forums and social groups.
Track engagement and signup conversions.
firstTenPlaybook.successMetric: Measure site traffic and trial signups from content.

firstTenPlaybook.title: GDPR Consultant Referral Program

recommendation.text: Reach out to GDPR consultants with proposal for referrals to compliant form solutions.

steps: List potential GDPR consultants.
Send partnership emails
Offer client trial accounts.
Measure referral counts.
firstTenPlaybook.successMetric: At least one referral partnership established.

thirtyDayPlan.objective: Prepare and run direct email outreach to small business owners.
actions: Compile prospects list of small business owners.
thirtyDayPlan.successMetric: Receive minimum 2 positive replies or signups.

rationale.text: Direct email is low-cost and immediate for validating demand with small business owners.

thirtyDayPlan.objective: Analyze email outreach results and decide next steps.
actions: If success metric met, plan scaling of outreach.
If not, prepare content marketing or partnership outreach.
thirtyDayPlan.successMetric: Decision whether to continue, pivot, or stop direct email outreach.

rationale.text: First test informs viability of small business outreach before more resource-intensive methods.

thirtyDayPlan.objective: Launch content marketing if pivoted from outreach failure.
actions: Write blog posts focused on marketing use cases.
Share posts in relevant communities and forums.
thirtyDayPlan.successMetric: Significant site traffic and trial signups from content.

rationale.text: Content appeals to marketing teams with form variety, expanding customer base prospect.

thirtyDayPlan.objective: Initiate GDPR consultant partnership outreach if content marketing insufficient.
actions: Offer free trials for their clients.
thirtyDayPlan.successMetric: At least one GDPR consultant partner secured.

firstExperiment.problem: Need professional, easy forms without coding or cost barriers
firstExperiment.identifyProspects: Use LinkedIn and local business directories to find small business owners.
firstExperiment.channelRationale: Allows personalized messaging highlighting free, simple form creation and immediate outreach with zero spend.
firstExperiment.firstAction: Send 5 personalized emails to selected prospects.

resources.assumptions: Prospect email contacts can be found publicly or via LinkedIn. Email volume is low for manual effort.

firstExperiment.commercialLearning: Measure reply rate and conversion to form signups to validate interest among small business owners.
firstExperiment.continueWhen: At least 2 positive replies or signups from 5 emails within 2 weeks.
firstExperiment.adjustWhen: Less than 2 positives but some engagement; consider content marketing targeting marketing teams.
firstExperiment.stopWhen: No replies or signups after 5 emails within 2 weeks; test next segment.

strongestAlternative.whyNotSelected: Content creation and distribution are more time-consuming with delayed feedback.
strongestAlternative.preferWhen: Small business owners poorly responsive to cold email and better reached via content.
